summary: Read a binary tree whose nodes each store an integer. Imagine an observer standing on the tree's right and looking left. On one level, a node farther right hides whatever sits behind it. Keep only the first node the gaze meets on that level. Write those integers from the upper level downward. An empty tree produces an empty result. If a left-hand node is the only one that reaches a deeper level, that deeper node still counts as seen and must be written.
notes: Compare after trimming trailing newlines. The input is a level-order node count, using a dot for a missing child.
